problems: The blind guess (a four-legged dog or cat, or a frog) does not match the Hanging Hawk. The bird reading only appears as a secondary alternative, so the silhouette does not read as a bird at first glance.
The figure is upright, with the head at top and the forked tail at bottom, so it is the right way round. It does not read as hanging, though.
The silhouette is thin and wiry. The body between the shoulders (crown, right shoulder, vent) is narrow, so the figure reads as a stick outline rather than a bird's body.
The hooked beak is not visible. The crown star (63462) sits at the top of a loop, with no beak shape beside it.
Labels collide: 'left wingtip (brightest star' overlaps 'inner bone of the left wing', and 'right shoulder, where the chest' overlaps 'right wing root'. Several labels are cut off at the frame edge.
The gold lines form a straight-edged polygon over the blue outline. The blue outline is a real silhouette, but the gold polygon dominates it, so the figure reads partly as a copy of the gold lines.
Star placement is broadly on the intended parts: the two tail prongs (61418, 63355) and the vent (62886) form a clear fork, and the wingtips sit at the outer extremes of the wings.
output.advice: Redraw so the silhouette reads as a bird first. (1) Widen the body: make the chest between the right shoulder (62763) and the vent (62886) fuller, and bring the left wing's inner bone (64022) closer to the body. (2) Add a hooked beak at the crown (63462), extending the head outward so the hook is visible. (3) Keep the left wingtip (64394) and right wingtip (59847) at the outer extremes, with the right tip drooping below the left. (4) Keep the forked tail with prongs 61418 and 63355 splayed clearly apart from the vent. (5) Offset labels with leader lines so 64394 and 64022 don't collide, and 62763 and 60742 don't collide, and keep every label inside the frame. (6) Reduce the gold polygon to a thin accent over a fuller blue silhouette, so the outline carries the shape.
